# Original runtime signature observations

The inert [archive](first.tar.xz), [index](index.json) and
[validation record](validation.json) retain 93 original records. Seven complete
projects have fourteen actual ordinary/selected CLI observations: ordinary
enum/match controls succeed, quantum nominal execution reaches its concrete
profile barriers, and ordinary quantum inspection/hidden observation reach
their actual type/effect errors. The prior CLI and native executables are
hash-bound observations, without current-head build attestation.

The new internal reader retains complete runtime prefixes around quantum
owners, including nested products and ordinary zero-width parameters. It reuses
the original finite-type and import readers; an annotation read is not a checked
body effect. The first reserved `Type` identifier error and separate default-list
projection error remain unchanged. Separate repairs compile with strict package
options; 22 small kernel reductions and a 21,130-declaration audit pass using
only the existing standard axiom basis. Single-process peak memory is about
1.65 GiB. No maximum-size quantum case is generated.

Original observers, source objects, complete diagnostic streams and source/import
maps remain inert data. Passive tests neither extract nor replay them. These
component compiles use stable existing imports and do not establish a full
dependency replay, source-body theorem or native execution gate. Current proof
records require genuine maintenance for this candidate. Ordinary/selected typed
execution, complete body/code/effect binding and generic/static transport remain
unfinished; #64 and #195 remain open.

The archived observer initially reports 23 reductions; enumerating the actual
theorem declarations gives 22. The separate validation record corrects that
count without rewriting the original observer or its archive.
